text:
# Successor to the construct, with the criticism carried

I am answering the criticism on its own terms: only where the substantive reason warrants a change do I revise; otherwise I preserve the construct and explain why the objection does not establish the defect. I keep the frozen P7 excerpt, the frozen P9 excerpt, the operator contract, the construct occurrence, and the criticism occurrence as distinct historical occurrences; nothing here is installed in the frozen carrier. The proposed successor below is a separate proposed object.

## 1. What I accept from the criticism

The criticism makes one specific, textual claim I think is established by the frozen material rather than merely proposed. P7's target list runs:

> "One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking's history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful."

The last item is not a record, a history, or an aggregate. It is a background presupposition under which the other items are read. P9's correlation objection concerns "a physical resource not named in the snapshot" — that is, a presupposition about which shared constraints the snapshot is taken to model, not a further fact about the snapshot's contents. So the construct's "bound-correspondence target" has a better home in P7's taxonomy as a criticism of a *source assumption* than as a subdivision of the snapshot-as-a-whole target. The construct said:

> "I propose that the correlation objection actually splits P7's 'snapshot-as-a-whole' target into two further targets…"

and did not notice that P7 already supplies a distinct slot for assumptions about what the snapshot models. That is a real defect, not a stylistic choice: it collapses a distinction P7 was careful to draw.

I also accept the smaller follow-on: when the construct says its construction "moves [the E009 item] to the front and says which half of P9 it belongs to," it has not yet settled which half, because it has not yet settled whether the correspondence side is a target inside the availability account or a source assumption outside it. That is an unfinished move, and the criticism correctly names it.

And I accept the third observation: P9's downstream-resolution criticism ("exposing alternatives without a policy for resolving them pushes the problem downstream, where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently") and P9's correlation objection do not belong to the same layer. The first is about entitlement of downstream consumers; the second is about correspondence between the modeled interval and a realizable joint set. The construct's re-description reply — "this is not a new language component… availability names the interval over the product of per-booking possibility sets" — can absorb the correlation objection under a stipulation, but it does not absorb the downstream-resolution objection. Presenting them as one layer loses that distinction.

## 2. What I do not accept, and why

The criticism's strongest move is its re-location of the correspondence side to the source-assumption slot. I accept that as the better reading, but I do not accept the implication that this makes the construct's *guiding question* moot, or that the construct's arithmetic-side / correspondence-side split is therefore unsupported. The criticism's own Objection 3, restated, says P7's list may be exhaustive in a local sense; the construct flagged exactly that and declined to resolve it. The criticism takes the flag and treats it as an unacknowledged revision. It is acknowledged. The construct says:

> "If someone thinks P7's list of targets is exhaustive and indivisible, the split is a disagreement with P7's taxonomy, not with P9's objection. I flag this rather than resolve it."

So the defect is not that the construct proceeded as if the split were a reading of P7. The defect is that the construct, having flagged the issue, continued to use the phrase "subdivision of snapshot-as-a-whole" in later sections as if the flag had been resolved in favor of the subdivision reading. I accept *that* — the inconsistency between the flag and later usage. I do not accept that the split itself is unsupported, only that its *classification* was left ambiguous.

On the second defect, I partially accept. The construct says E009 "does not engage P9's correspondence-side objection, because WHL has no primitive for joint realizability beyond the capacity sum." That is accurate. The criticism's point that "which half of P9 it belongs to is exactly the question the construct has not settled" is fair as stated, but the construct's sentence is also readable as an observation that the E009 item *can* be assigned either way depending on the reading — and that this is itself the open question. The construct could have been clearer. I accept the clarification, not the charge of error.

On the third point — the different direction of the correlation objection and the downstream-resolution objection — I accept it as a genuine improvement, not as a defect in the construct. The construct did not say they were the same layer; it discussed them in adjacent sections and treated both as elements of P9. But the criticism sharpens the distinction, and I incorporate that sharpening below.

## 3. The successor: re-classification, not subdivision

The successor preserves the construct's substantive split between bound-arithmetic and bound-correspondence readings of the correlation objection. It changes the classification of the second half, and it distinguishes the two P9 objections by layer.

**Successor claim S1 (re-classification).** The bound-arithmetic target is a criticism of a reconstruction rule — specifically, of the rule that the availability interval for a snapshot is [capacity − Σ per-booking maximum, capacity − Σ per-booking minimum], read as an arithmetic claim over the product of per-booking possibility sets. The bound-correspondence target is not a subdivision of the snapshot-as-a-whole target; it is a criticism of a source assumption, namely the assumption that capacity is the only shared constraint that bears on joint realizability. This places the correspondence side in the slot P7 already provides ("the assumption that logical time is meaningful" and, by extension, other source assumptions about what the snapshot models), rather than manufacturing a new sub-target inside "snapshot as a whole."

**Successor claim S2 (layered objections).** P9's correlation objection and P9's downstream-resolution objection are criticisms at different layers, with different scope:

- The correlation objection can be absorbed by stipulation: if "availability" names the interval over the modeled product set, no correspondence claim is made, and no change to the arithmetic is required. The objection then only bites if someone claims the interval characterizes the warehouse, not the model. Under P7's taxonomy, the claim that it characterizes the warehouse is a claim about a source assumption, not about the availability account's internal arithmetic.
- The downstream-resolution objection cannot be absorbed by stipulation. It is a criticism of the practice of exposing unresolved alternatives without a resolution policy, and it concerns the entitlement of consumers to infer commitments from the exposure. Under P7's taxonomy, it targets the snapshot-as-a-whole as a *presentation*, not as a model, and it does not reduce to the correlation objection.

**Successor claim S3 (preserved construct content).** The following construct claims are preserved without change, because the criticism does not establish a defect in them:

- The distinction between the two halves of P9's correlation objection (arithmetic vs correspondence).
- The observation that the arithmetic can be correct while a correspondence claim fails, because the per-booking possibility sets need not be projections of any joint possibility set.
- The candid acknowledgment that the correspondence failure only matters if a reader cares about physical realizability, and that P9's example is an illustration rather than a case.
- The observation that E009's proposed repair "add resource model or possible-worlds set" names the correspondence side, and that E009 treats it as one item in a list.
- The observation that P9's correlation objection would survive any repair of WHL's availability-bound naming.

**Successor claim S4 (what remains an open interpretive question).** Whether P7's "snapshot as a whole" was meant broadly enough to include the snapshot's implicit modeling commitments. The construct flagged this; the criticism notes it; the successor leaves it unresolved and says so. The successor's re-classification (S1) is a proposed reading, not a stipulation about P7's intent.

## 4. Answering the guiding question under the successor

The contract's guiding question is: does P9's compatibility objection require any change to an account of global availability, and if so what is being questioned in P7's sense?

Under the successor:

- **No change to the availability arithmetic** is required by the correlation objection alone. The arithmetic over the modeled product set is well-defined and can be reported. This is preserved from the construct.
- **A change to a claim about correspondence** is required only if the account is read as claiming that the interval characterizes the warehouse. Under P7's taxonomy, this is not a criticism of the availability rule; it is a criticism of a source assumption about what the snapshot models.
- **A change to the availability account's presentation** may be required by the downstream-resolution objection, but that objection is about entitlement, not about arithmetic, and it is not settled by the correlation objection. This is the layered-objections point (S2) the construct did not draw.

So the successor's answer to the guiding question is: the compatibility objection is a criticism of a source assumption, not of the availability account's internal arithmetic. Under the arithmetic-side reading, it changes nothing in the account. Under the correspondence-side reading, it changes which claim is being made, not how the arithmetic is done. The E009 criticism's repairs to WHL's naming address the arithmetic side and do not engage either the correspondence side or the downstream-resolution side. The E009 criticism's proposed repair "add a resource model or possible-worlds set" names the correspondence side but does not decide whether it belongs to the availability account or to a source assumption, and the E009 criticism does not raise the downstream-resolution objection at all.

## 5. What remains protected after the successor

The contract's protected distinctions are preserved and their locations named:

- **Criticizing a rule vs. criticizing its records**: preserved. In the successor's classification, the arithmetic side is a criticism of a rule (the interval rule); the source-assumption side is not a criticism of a record.
- **Different combinations of accepting/rejecting rule and data**: preserved, and now located. Rejecting the arithmetic rule while accepting the records is a rule criticism. Accepting the arithmetic rule while rejecting the data as corrupt or late is a data criticism. The correspondence claim is neither: it is a claim about what the snapshot models.
- **Cross-booking incompatibility as conditional possibility, not observation**: preserved. P9 says "might be incompatible"; the successor's correspondence side is conditional on the same premise.
- **Local alternatives, aggregation, bounds, correlation objections as different roles**: preserved with the layering (S2). Local alternatives drive the per-booking possibility set; aggregation produces the interval; the correlation objection is the claim that the interval may not correspond; the downstream-resolution objection is the claim that exposure without policy shifts the problem.
- **Exposing alternatives vs. objecting to downstream resolution as disputed positions**: preserved. The successor does not resolve the dispute; it locates it at a different layer from the correlation objection.
- **No endorsement of the missing constraint**: preserved. The successor's correspondence side is conditional on a premise the packet does not assert.

## 6. What observation or interpretation would matter, under the successor

The successor's S1 and S2 are decided by observation in the same way the construct's split was:

- S1 (re-classification) is decided by textual reading of P7. Under the broad reading of "snapshot as a whole," the construct's original subdivision holds and the successor's re-classification fails. Under the narrow reading, the successor's re-classification holds. The successor notes this (S4) rather than resolving it.
- S2 (layering) is decided by whether the correlation objection and the downstream-resolution objection can be separated. If someone argues they are the same objection under different descriptions, S2 fails. The construct's argument was that they belong to adjacent sections of P9; the criticism sharpened this by showing they pull in different directions (one absorbable by stipulation, one not). The successor adopts the sharpening.

The further observation that would settle the original split remains the same: a snapshot plus an unstated resource model where the per-booking possibility sets have a product set strictly larger than the realizable set. Without such a case, the correspondence side is a distinction in search of an instance. Under the successor's re-classification, this observation would settle a claim about a source assumption, not a claim about the availability account's internal coherence — which is what the criticism said the construct should have noticed.

## 7. What I am not claiming

I am not claiming that the successor's re-classification is forced by P7. It is a proposed reading, and the broad reading remains open. I am not claiming that the successor's S2 layering is forced by P9. P9 discusses the two objections in adjacent sentences and does not itself italicize their difference in direction. I am not claiming that the E009 criticism's repairs are wrong or unhelpful; I am claiming they address the arithmetic side and not the correspondence side or the downstream-resolution side. I am not claiming that the construct's central split was false, only that its classification of the second half was left ambiguous in a way the criticism correctly identifies.

The proposed successor artifact is the re-classification S1, the layering S2, the preservations S3, and the open question S4, expressed in prose above. It is not installed in the frozen carrier. It is a separate proposed object.
